# Go standard

<!-- Sources:
[effective-go] Effective Go — https://go.dev/doc/effective_go
[review] Go Code Review Comments — https://go.dev/wiki/CodeReviewComments
[test-comments] Go Test Comments — https://go.dev/wiki/TestComments
[doc-comments] Go Doc Comments — https://go.dev/doc/comment
[errors] Working with Errors in Go 1.13 — https://go.dev/blog/go1.13-errors
[context] Go Concurrency Patterns: Context — https://go.dev/blog/context
[layout] Organizing a Go module — https://go.dev/doc/modules/layout
[sql-injection] Avoiding SQL injection risk — https://go.dev/doc/database/sql-injection
-->

## Summary

- Follow the repo's existing layout, module structure and conventions; these defaults apply only where the repo has none.
- Code is `gofmt`-clean and passes `go vet`, the repo's linter and `go test -race`: no data races, no leaked goroutines.
- Names are short MixedCaps with uniform initialisms (`userID`, `ServeHTTP`); package names are lowercase single words, never repeated in identifiers.
- Check every error; wrap with `%w` only when callers may inspect the cause; test with `errors.Is`/`errors.As`; error strings lowercase, unpunctuated.
- `context.Context` is the first parameter, named `ctx`, never stored in a struct; every goroutine has a known exit.
- Define small interfaces where they are consumed; return concrete types; make the zero value useful.
- Tests use the standard `testing` package, table-driven where cases share logic; failure messages name the function, input, got, then want.

## Layout and packages

<!-- [layout] internal, cmd; [effective-go] Package names; [review] Package Names, Imports, Import Blank, Import Dot -->
- Keep the existing module layout, package boundaries and naming even where they differ from this file. <!-- factory -->
- New code defaults to `internal/`; executables go in `cmd/<name>/main.go` when a repo has several commands or mixes commands and libraries.
- Package names: short, lowercase, one word, no underscores or mixedCaps, equal to the directory's base name. Never `util`, `common`, `misc`, `helpers`.
- Don't repeat the package name in its identifiers: `bufio.Reader`, not `bufio.BufReader`; `ring.New`, not `ring.NewRing`.
- Rename an import only on a collision, renaming the more local one. No dot imports; blank (`_`) imports only in `main` or tests.

## Naming

<!-- [effective-go] Names, Getters, Interface names, MixedCaps; [review] Initialisms, Mixed Caps, Receiver Names, Variable Names -->
- MixedCaps or mixedCaps, never underscores; unexported constants are `maxLength`, not `MAX_LENGTH`.
- Initialisms keep one case throughout: `URL`/`url`, `HTTPClient`, `appID`; never `Url`, `Id`, `Http`.
- Getters drop `Get` (`Owner()`, `SetOwner(o)`). Single-method interfaces are method name plus `-er` (`Reader`). Use `Read`, `Write`, `String`, `Close` only with their standard signature and meaning (`String()`, not `ToString()`).
- Receiver names are one or two letters derived from the type (`c` for `Client`), identical across all methods; never `this`, `self`, `me`. Local names shrink with their scope (`i`, `buf`).

## Control flow and functions

<!-- [effective-go] Formatting, If, Multiple return values, Named result parameters, Defer; [review] Gofmt, Indent Error Flow, Line Length, Naked Returns, Named Result Parameters, In-Band Errors, Synchronous Functions -->
- `gofmt -l` must print nothing; run `goimports` if available. No hard line limit unless the repo's linter sets one; break at logical points.
- Handle the error or special case first and return; keep the success path unindented and drop `else` after a `return`. Scope values in the statement: `if err := f(); err != nil {`.
- Return `error` (or `ok bool`) as the last result instead of in-band sentinels like `-1`, `""` or `nil`.
- Name results only when they document (two results of one type) or a deferred closure must set them; bare `return` only in short functions.
- Release resources with `defer` right after the successful acquire: `defer f.Close()` follows the `err` check.

## Types, interfaces and values

<!-- [effective-go] Data, Interfaces, Interface checks, Pointers vs. Values; [review] Interfaces, Receiver Type, Copying, Pass Values, Declaring Empty Slices -->
- Declare interfaces in the package that uses them, listing only the methods it calls. Producers return concrete types (usually struct pointers). No interfaces just for mocking.
- Assert interface satisfaction at compile time when nothing else would: `var _ io.Writer = (*Buffer)(nil)`.
- Design the zero value to be usable (`sync.Mutex`, `bytes.Buffer` need no init); add `NewT` only when setup is required.
- Pointer receivers when a method mutates, the struct holds a `sync.Mutex` or is large; value receivers for small immutable types. Don't mix both on one type, don't copy such values, and don't pass `*string` or `*io.Reader` to save bytes.
- Declare empty slices as `var s []T`; use `[]T{}` only when encoding must emit `[]`. APIs must not treat nil and empty slices differently.
- Use a concrete type or type parameter instead of `any` when the type is known. No mutable package-level state; `init()` only registers. <!-- factory -->

## Errors

<!-- [errors] Errors in Go 1.13, Whether to Wrap, Errors and package APIs; [effective-go] Errors; [review] Handle Errors, Error Strings; [test-comments] Test Error Semantics -->
- Check every returned error; never discard one with `_`. Check the `Close` error of files you wrote.
- Add context naming the operation and input; error strings are lowercase with no trailing punctuation and may carry an origin prefix (`"config: missing key"`).
- Use `%w` when callers should be able to inspect the cause; wrapping makes the cause part of your API. Use `%v` to hide implementation details such as a driver's error.
- Inspect errors with `errors.Is` (values) and `errors.As` (types), never `==`, type assertions or string matching.
- Export a sentinel (`var ErrNotFound = errors.New("store: not found")`) or error type only when callers must branch on it; document which errors a function returns.
- Handle an error once: return it or log it, not both. <!-- factory -->
```go
if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
	return defaults, nil
}
if err != nil {
	return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("load config %q: %w", path, err)
}
```

## Panics

<!-- [effective-go] Panic, Recover; [review] Don't Panic -->
- Return errors for anything that can fail at runtime; never use `panic` for ordinary error handling or control flow.
- Panic only on impossible states (programmer errors) or failed initialisation, e.g. compiling a constant regexp at package level.
- A panic must not leave a package's exported API: if a package panics internally, `recover` in a deferred function at the entry point and return an `error`.

## Concurrency and context

<!-- [context] all; [review] Contexts, Goroutine Lifetimes, Synchronous Functions; [effective-go] Concurrency, Share by communicating -->
- Every function on a request path, doing I/O, or that may block takes `ctx context.Context` first: `func (c *Client) Get(ctx context.Context, id string)`.
- Never store a context in a struct or define custom context types; pass it explicitly.
- Call the `cancel` from `WithCancel`/`WithTimeout` with `defer`; when `ctx.Done()` closes, stop work and return `ctx.Err()` (wrapped). Context values: request-scoped data only, unexported key type.
- Prefer synchronous functions; let callers add concurrency. Before starting a goroutine know how it ends (context, closed channel, `WaitGroup`); a goroutine blocked forever on a channel is a leak.
- "Share memory by communicating"; otherwise guard shared state with a mutex.
- Code must be race-free under `go test -race`. Pass `context.TODO()`, never `nil`. Only senders close channels. Use `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup` only if `go.mod` already requires it. <!-- factory -->
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := c.do(ctx, req)
```

## Doc comments

<!-- [doc-comments] General rules, Package, Command, Type, Func, Syntax; [review] Doc Comments, Comment Sentences, Package Comments, Examples -->
- Every exported name, and every non-trivial unexported type or function, has a doc comment directly above it, no blank line between. Write full sentences that start with the name: `// Fetch returns ...`; boolean functions "report whether ...".
- Package comment `// Package store ...` sits directly above `package` in exactly one file; for `main` it starts with the command name.
- Type comments say what a value represents, what its zero value means if not obvious, and whether it is safe for concurrent use.
- Say what and why, not how the algorithm works. Mark replacements with a `Deprecated:` paragraph; link names as `[io.Reader]`.

## Untrusted input

<!-- [sql-injection]; [review] Crypto Rand; [effective-go] A web server (html/template) -->
- Pass values as query arguments with the driver's placeholder (`?`, `$1`); never build SQL with `fmt.Sprintf` or `+`.
- Run programs as `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "log", ref)`; never pass user input through `sh -c` or any shell. <!-- factory -->
- Generate keys, tokens and nonces with `crypto/rand`, never `math/rand`. Render HTML with `html/template`, not `text/template`, so input is escaped.
- Never log secrets, tokens, passwords or credential-bearing headers or bodies. <!-- factory -->
- Validate input at the boundary (handler, flag parsing). Set timeouts on `http.Server` and `http.Client`; always close response bodies. <!-- factory -->

## Tests

<!-- [test-comments] all sections; [review] Useful Test Failures -->
- Tests live in `_test.go` files beside the code; fixtures go under `testdata/`. Match the repo's choice of `package foo` vs `package foo_test`. <!-- factory -->
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test or subtest whose name mentions the scenario. <!-- factory -->
- Use the standard `testing` package; no assertion libraries unless the repo already uses one.
- Use a table with `t.Run` when cases share checking logic; write separate tests when the logic differs. Subtest names stay readable. New packages get a runnable `Example`.
- Failure messages name the function and input, then got before want: `Parse(%q) = %v, want %v`.
- Prefer `t.Error` so one run reports every failure; `t.Fatal` only when setup fails or the rest cannot proceed, and only on the test goroutine.
- Compare whole values. Use `cmp.Diff` with a `(-want +got)` key if `go.mod` already requires go-cmp; else `reflect.DeepEqual`, `slices.Equal`. Never add dependencies from tests. <!-- factory -->
- Check errors with `errors.Is`/`errors.As`, or just `err != nil` when the API exposes no structure; never compare error text. Decode JSON before comparing rather than matching bytes.
- Call `t.Helper()` in setup helpers, but don't build assert-style helpers. Use `t.TempDir`, `t.Cleanup`, `httptest`; `t.Parallel()` only without shared state; never `time.Sleep` to synchronise. <!-- factory -->
```go
t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) { // inside: for _, tc := range tests
	if got := Parse(tc.in); got != tc.want {
		t.Errorf("Parse(%q) = %v, want %v", tc.in, got, tc.want)
	}
})
```

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `*_test.go`
- `testdata/*`
- `*/testdata/*`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `out="$(gofmt -l .)"; [ -z "$out" ] || { echo "needs gofmt:"; echo "$out"; exit 1; }`
- lint: `golangci-lint run`
- types: `go vet ./...`
- test: `go test -race ./...`
- testAffected: `go test -race {packages}`

# Helm / Kubernetes standard

<!-- Sources:
[helm-bp] Helm Chart Best Practices — https://helm.sh/docs/chart_best_practices/
[helm-charts] Charts (Chart.yaml, Dependencies, CRDs) — https://helm.sh/docs/topics/charts/
[helm-schema] Charts: Schema Files — https://helm.sh/docs/topics/charts/#schema-files
[helm-tips] Chart Development Tips and Tricks — https://helm.sh/docs/howto/charts_tips_and_tricks/
[helm-funcs] Template Function List — https://helm.sh/docs/chart_template_guide/function_list/
[helm-tests] Chart Tests — https://helm.sh/docs/topics/chart_tests/
[helm-unittest] helm-unittest README and test API — https://github.com/helm-unittest/helm-unittest
[k8s-config] Configuration Good Practices — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/overview/
[k8s-images] Images — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/
[k8s-resources] Resource Management for Pods and Containers — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/
[pss] Pod Security Standards — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/
[probes] Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes — https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/
[probes-concept] Liveness, Readiness, and Startup Probes — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/liveness-readiness-startup-probes/
[labels] Recommended Labels — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/common-labels/
[k8s-rbac] Role Based Access Control Good Practices — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/rbac-good-practices/
-->

## Summary

- Keep the repo's chart layout, naming and value structure; `Chart.yaml` uses `apiVersion: v2` and a SemVer 2 `version`.
- Values are camelCase, strings quoted, every key commented starting with its name, and typed in `values.schema.json`.
- `values.schema.json` is a contract: update it with every values change and keep it backwards compatible unless the spec says otherwise.
- Templates use chart-prefixed `define` names, `include … | nindent`, `required` for mandatory values, and standard labels on every resource.
- Containers meet the restricted Pod Security Standard, pin image tags (never `latest`), set requests and limits, and define probes.
- No secret values in values, templates or tests; reference existing Secrets by name.
- Every spec scenario has a named helm-unittest test in `tests/*_test.yaml`; alternative configurations live in `ci/*-values.yaml`.

## Chart metadata and dependencies

<!-- [helm-bp] General Conventions; Templates: Structure of templates/; Dependencies; Custom Resource Definitions; [helm-charts] The Chart.yaml File, Chart Dependencies, Limitations on CRDs; [helm-tips] Partials -->
- Keep the repo's existing chart layout, file names and value structure where they differ from this standard. <!-- factory -->
- Use `apiVersion: v2`. Chart names: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, alphanumeric at both ends, ≤ 63 characters.
- `version` is SemVer 2; `appVersion` tracks the application independently and is quoted (`appVersion: "1.0"`).
- Bump `version` with every change to the chart. <!-- factory -->
- Indent YAML with two spaces, never tabs. New templates: `.yaml` for manifests, `.tpl` for helpers, dashed names that include the kind (`api-service.yaml`), one resource per file; helpers go in `_helpers.tpl`.
- Declare dependencies with patch-level ranges (`version: ~1.2.3`) and `https://` repositories; gate optional ones with `condition: <name>.enabled`.
- Put CRDs as plain YAML (no template directives) in `crds/` or a separate chart; Helm installs them once and never upgrades or deletes them.

## Values and schema

<!-- [helm-bp] Values: Naming Conventions, Flat or Nested Values, Make Types Clear, Consider How Users Will Use Your Values, Document values.yaml; [helm-schema]; [k8s-config] General configuration tips -->
- Name keys camelCase starting lowercase (`serverPort`, not `ServerPort`/`server-port`); read dashed subchart keys with `index .Values "sub-chart" "key"`.
- Prefer flat keys; nest only a group of related settings where at least one is mandatory.
- Quote string values; leave ints and booleans bare; write booleans only as `true`/`false`; store large integers as strings and convert with `int`.
- Prefer maps keyed by name over lists of objects so `--set servers.foo.port=80` keeps working.
- Comment every key, starting with the key name: `# replicaCount is the number of pods the Deployment runs.`
- The schema validates the merged values, subchart schemas included, on install, upgrade, `helm lint` and `helm template`.
- Change `values.schema.json` in the same commit as any values change: type each new key; add `enum`, `minimum` or `pattern` where meaningful. <!-- factory -->
- Do not remove, rename or narrow existing values; add new ones as optional with defaults that keep current output, unless the spec says otherwise. <!-- factory -->
- Never put secret values in `values.yaml`, templates, tests or `ci/` files; take an existing Secret's name and use `secretKeyRef`/`envFrom`. <!-- factory -->

## Templates

<!-- [helm-bp] Templates: Names of Defined Templates, Formatting Templates, Comments; [helm-tips] Quote Strings, include, required, Automatically Roll Deployments; [helm-funcs] fail, nindent -->
- Prefix every `define` with the chart name (`"mychart.fullname"`, never `"fullname"`); defined templates are global across parent and subcharts.
- Call helpers with `include`, not `template`, so output can be piped; render nested values with `toYaml` and `nindent`:

```yaml
  labels:
    {{- include "mychart.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  resources:
    {{- toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 4 }}
```

- Write `{{ .Values.x }}` with inner spaces; chomp with `{{-`/`-}}`, but chomping both sides can join lines, so check rendered output.
- Pipe strings through `quote`; leave integers unquoted (env var `value`s are strings, so quote them).
- Fail early: `required "image.repository is required" .Values.image.repository` for mandatory values, `fail` for invalid combinations.
- Document helpers with `{{- /* … */ -}}` comments; never put `required` inside a `#` YAML comment, which still renders.
- Roll pods on config change with `checksum/config: {{ include (print $.Template.BasePath "/configmap.yaml") . | sha256sum }}`.

## Labels and selectors

<!-- [helm-bp] Labels and Annotations: Standard Labels; Pods and PodTemplates: PodTemplates Should Declare Selectors; [labels]; [k8s-config] Working with labels -->
- Build labels in one `<chart>.labels` helper applied to every resource: `app.kubernetes.io/name`, `app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}`, `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: {{ .Release.Service }}`, `helm.sh/chart: {{ .Chart.Name }}-{{ .Chart.Version | replace "+" "_" }}`; add `version`, `component`, `part-of` where meaningful.
- Use labels only for metadata used to select or query; everything else, including Helm hooks, is an annotation.
- Give every PodTemplate an explicit `selector` from stable labels (`name`, `instance`); never select on `version` or `helm.sh/chart`.

## Images and resources

<!-- [helm-bp] Pods and PodTemplates: Images, ImagePullPolicy; [k8s-images] Image pull policy; [k8s-resources] Requests and limits, Resource units -->
- Take `image.repository`, `image.tag` (or digest) and `image.pullPolicy` from values; default to a fixed tag or digest, never `latest`, `head` or `canary`.
- Default `pullPolicy: IfNotPresent`; if omitted, Kubernetes uses `Always` for `latest` or untagged images and never revisits it after creation.
- Set CPU and memory `requests` and `limits` from values. Requests drive scheduling; a lone limit also becomes the request; CPU over limit is throttled, memory over limit is OOM-killed.
- Write CPU as millicores (`250m`) and memory as `Mi`/`Gi`; lowercase `m` on memory means millibytes (`400m` is 0.4 bytes).

## Probes

<!-- [probes]; [probes-concept] -->
- Define a readiness probe so Services route traffic only to ready pods; it runs for the container's whole life.
- A liveness probe must signal only unrecoverable failure (e.g. a deadlock); one that fails under load causes cascading restarts.
- For slow starters add a `startupProbe` with `failureThreshold × periodSeconds` ≥ worst-case startup; liveness and readiness wait for it. Point `httpGet`/`tcpSocket` probes at named ports.

## Pod security and RBAC

<!-- [pss] Baseline and Restricted policies; [k8s-config] Managing workloads, hostPort and hostNetwork; [helm-bp] Role-Based Access Control; [k8s-rbac] Least privilege -->
- Every container, init containers included, meets the restricted profile:

```yaml
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
  capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
```

- Never set `runAsUser: 0` or `privileged: true`; add no capability except `NET_BIND_SERVICE`.
- No `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`, `hostIPC`, `hostPort` or `hostPath`; use only configMap, secret, emptyDir, projected, downwardAPI, csi, ephemeral or persistentVolumeClaim volumes.
- Run pods through a controller (Deployment, StatefulSet, Job), never as naked Pods.
- Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` unless the workload calls the Kubernetes API.
- Keep `rbac.create` (boolean, default `true`) separate from `serviceAccount.create` and `serviceAccount.name`; resolve the name in a `<chart>.serviceAccountName` helper (set name, else fullname if created, else `default`).
- Grant least privilege: namespaced `Role`/`RoleBinding` over cluster-wide ones, only needed verbs and resources, no `*` wildcards, never `cluster-admin`.

## Tests

<!-- [helm-unittest] README, DOCUMENT.md assertion types; [helm-tests] -->
- Unit tests are helm-unittest suites in `tests/*_test.yaml`; the tester may edit only these and `ci/*-values.yaml`. <!-- factory -->
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test whose `it:` is named after the scenario. <!-- factory -->
- Each test sets inputs via `set`/`values` and asserts specific paths (`equal`, `exists`, `notExists`, `contains`, `isKind`, `hasDocuments`); use `failedTemplate` for `required`, `fail` and schema errors.
- Every `ci/*-values.yaml` must render, pass the schema and validate with kubeconform. <!-- factory -->
- In-cluster `helm test` hooks are Pods/Jobs in `templates/tests/` annotated `"helm.sh/hook": test`; they pass on exit code 0.

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `tests/*_test.yaml`
- `*/tests/*_test.yaml`
- `ci/*-values.yaml`
- `*/ci/*-values.yaml`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `yamllint {charts}`
- lint: `helm lint {charts}`
- types: `for c in {charts}; do m="$(helm template "$c")" || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$m" | kubeconform -strict -summary || exit 1; done`
- test: `helm unittest {charts}`
- testAffected: `helm unittest {charts}`

## Summary

- Keep the repo's layout, tooling (uv/poetry/pip) and conventions; code must pass `ruff format`, `ruff check` and strict `pyright`/`mypy`.
- Follow PEP 8 naming; absolute imports grouped stdlib, third-party, local; no wildcard imports.
- Annotate every public function, including return types; use `X | None` and `list[int]`; avoid `Any`.
- Raise and catch specific exceptions, chain with `raise ... from`, keep `try` bodies small, never use bare `except:`.
- Log with `logging.getLogger(__name__)` and lazy `%s` arguments; never log secrets.
- Bind SQL parameters, pass subprocess arguments as lists, and never use `shell=True` with untrusted input.
- Test with pytest: plain `assert`, fixtures, `parametrize`, `tmp_path`, `monkeypatch`; name each test after its spec scenario.

## Project conventions

<!-- [pep20] explicit, simple, flat, easy to explain; [google-py] 3.17 Main -->
- Keep the existing package layout, dependency tool and conventions where they differ from this standard; add dependencies only through that tool. <!-- factory -->
- Let `ruff format` own layout; do not reformat or reorder code you did not change. <!-- factory -->
- Choose the explicit, flat, simple solution; if an implementation is hard to explain, redesign it.
- Put script behaviour in `main()` behind `if __name__ == "__main__":`; do nothing at import time beyond definitions.

## Naming

<!-- [pep8] Naming Conventions; [google-py] 3.16 Naming, 2.5 Mutable Global State -->
- `snake_case` for modules (no dashes), functions, methods and variables; `CapWords` for classes and type aliases.
- Exception classes end in `Error`; constants are module-level `UPPER_CASE`.
- One leading underscore marks non-public names; avoid `__mangled` names and mutable module-level state.
- Use descriptive names; single letters only for counters, `e` in handlers, `f` for files; never `l`, `O`, `I`.

## Imports

<!-- [pep8] Imports; [google-py] 2.2 Imports, 3.13 Imports formatting (stricter than pep8 on relative imports) -->
- Use absolute imports with the full package path; never `from module import *`.
- Imports go at the top after the module docstring, one per line, grouped `__future__`, stdlib, third-party, local, blank line between groups.
- Import abstract collection types (`Iterable`, `Mapping`, …) from `collections.abc`, not `typing`.

## Comparisons

<!-- [pep8] Programming Recommendations; [google-py] 2.14 True/False Evaluations -->
- Compare to `None` with `is` / `is not` (not `not x is None`); do not write `if x:` when you mean `if x is not None:`.
- Never compare booleans with `==`; test empty sequences with `if not seq:`, not `len(seq) == 0`.
- Use `isinstance()` rather than comparing `type()`; use `startswith()`/`endswith()` rather than slicing.

## Exceptions

<!-- [pep8] Programming Recommendations; [google-py] 2.4 Exceptions; [pep20] errors never pass silently -->
- Raise the most specific built-in (`ValueError` for bad arguments) or a project exception derived from `Exception`; name the failing value in the message.
- Catch only what you can handle; never bare `except:`. Catch `Exception` only to re-raise or at a deliberate isolation point that logs.
- Keep the `try` body to the statement that can fail; follow-up code goes in `else`, cleanup in `finally`.
- Chain translated errors so the cause survives:

  ```python
  try:
      port = int(raw)
  except ValueError as e:
      raise ConfigError(f"invalid port {raw!r}") from e
  ```
- Do not use `assert` for runtime checks in production code; raise instead.

## Functions and data

<!-- [google-py] 2.12 Default Argument Values, 2.13 Properties; [pep8] Programming Recommendations; [dataclasses] -->
- Never use a mutable default (list, dict, set, object); default to `None` and build it inside:

  ```python
  def add(item: str, bucket: list[str] | None = None) -> list[str]:
      if bucket is None:
          bucket = []
  ```
- Return consistently: every path returns a value (an explicit `return None` included) or none does. Use `def`, not a named lambda.
- Use `@dataclass` for records, `frozen=True` for values, `field(default_factory=list)` for mutable fields, `__post_init__` for validation.
- Use `@property` only for cheap, attribute-like computation; prefer a public attribute over a trivial getter/setter.
- Manage files, sockets, locks and connections with `with`; use `contextlib.closing()` for objects that lack context-manager support.

## Typing

<!-- [typing] Ergonomic Practices, Stylistic Practices; [pep484] The Any type; [google-py] 3.19 Type Annotations -->
- Annotate parameters and return types of every public function and method; unannotated parameters are implicit `Any`. <!-- factory -->
- Write `X | None` (None last) and `X | Y`, not `Optional`/`Union`; never rely on implicit optional (`x: str = None`).
- Use built-in generics (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, `type[C]`), not `typing.List` and friends.
- Accept broad types (`Iterable`, `Sequence`, `Mapping`, a `Protocol`); return concrete ones (`list`, `dict`).
- Annotate a parameter that takes any value as `object`; reserve `Any` for what the type system cannot express.
- Avoid union return types that force callers into `isinstance()` checks; use `typing.Protocol` for structural interfaces.
- Every `# type: ignore[code]` names its error code and gives a reason. <!-- factory -->

## Docstrings

<!-- [pep257] One-line, Multi-line Docstrings; [google-py] 3.8 Comments and Docstrings -->
- Give every public module, class, function and method a `"""triple-double-quoted"""` docstring.
- Open with a one-line imperative summary ending in a period ("Return the user ID."); do not restate the signature.
- Multi-line: summary, blank line, details, then `Args:`, `Returns:`/`Yields:`, `Raises:` where they add information; document constructors in `__init__`.

## Logging and strings

<!-- [logging] Advanced Logging Tutorial, Configuring Logging for a Library, Optimization, When to use logging; [google-py] 3.10 Strings -->
- One logger per module: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`; never log to the root logger in library code.
- Pass a constant format string plus arguments so formatting is deferred; no f-strings in logging calls:

  ```python
  logger.info("Loaded %d rows from %s", count, path)    # do
  logger.info(f"Loaded {count} rows from {path}")       # don't
  ```
- Call `logger.exception()` only inside `except`; choose the level by intent (debug, info, warning, error).
- Libraries add at most a `NullHandler`; only the application configures handlers. `print()` is for a CLI's user output only.
- Use f-strings for other formatting; accumulate strings with `"".join(...)`, not `+=` in a loop.

## Untrusted input

<!-- [subprocess] Security Considerations, Frequently Used Arguments; [sqlite3] placeholders; [pickle] warning; [secrets] -->
- Bind SQL values through the driver's placeholders (`cur.execute("... WHERE name = ?", (name,))`); never build SQL with f-strings, `%` or `+`. <!-- factory -->
- Run commands with an argument list and no shell; never `shell=True` with untrusted input. <!-- factory -->

  ```python
  subprocess.run(["git", "log", "--", user_path], check=True, timeout=30)
  ```
- Use `pathlib`, `glob` and `shutil` instead of shell pipelines and wildcards.
- Never unpickle data you did not produce: loading a pickle can run arbitrary code. Exchange data as JSON.
- Generate tokens, passwords and keys with `secrets` (`secrets.token_urlsafe()`), never `random`.
- Never log or print secrets, tokens, passwords or personal data, at any level. <!-- factory -->

## Testing

<!-- [pytest] Conventions for Python test discovery, Choosing a test layout; [pytest-fixtures]; [pytest-parametrize]; [pytest-assert]; [pytest-tmp-path]; [pytest-monkeypatch] -->
- Tests live only in `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `tests/` or `conftest.py`; the tester edits nothing else. <!-- factory -->
- Every spec scenario has at least one test named after it. <!-- factory -->
- Use `test_` functions or `Test` classes without `__init__`; follow the repo's existing test layout.
- Use plain `assert` (pytest shows operand values), `pytest.approx` for floats, `pytest.raises(Error, match=...)` around only the raising call.
- Inject setup via fixtures; tear down after `yield`; one state-changing action per fixture; share fixtures via `conftest.py`.
- Use `@pytest.mark.parametrize` for tables of cases instead of loops in a test:

  ```python
  @pytest.mark.parametrize(("raw", "expected"), [("1", 1), ("-2", -2)])
  def test_parse_int_accepts_signed_digits(raw: str, expected: int) -> None:
      assert parse_int(raw) == expected
  ```
- Use `tmp_path` (not `tmpdir`) for files and `monkeypatch` for env vars and attributes, patching the name where the code looks it up.
- Prefer passing dependencies in over patching; never patch builtins such as `open`.

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `test_*.py`
- `*/test_*.py`
- `*_test.py`
- `tests/*`
- `*/tests/*`
- `conftest.py`
- `*/conftest.py`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `ruff format --check .`
- lint: `ruff check .`
- types: `pyright` (with pyrightconfig.json); or `pyright` (when pyproject.toml has [tool.pyright]); or `mypy --strict .`
- test: `pytest`
- testAffected: `pytest {testFiles}`

## Summary

- Keep rendering pure: same props, state and context give the same JSX; side effects go in event handlers, effects only as last resort.
- Never mutate props, state, hook arguments or values already used in JSX; build new objects and update through the state setter.
- Call hooks only at the top level of components and custom hooks; keep `react-hooks` lint clean and never suppress `exhaustive-deps`.
- Derive values during render; use effects only to sync with external systems, with cleanup and every reactive dependency listed.
- Keep state minimal with one owner: no redundant, duplicated or contradictory state; lift to the closest common parent; reset with `key`.
- Keep the repo's structure, state library, styling and data layer; no untrusted `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; no secrets in client code.
- Test visible behaviour with Testing Library: `getByRole` first, `user-event` interactions, at least one test named after each spec scenario.

## Project and security

<!-- factory; [dom] dangerouslySetInnerHTML -->
- Keep the repo's existing component structure, state library, styling approach, data layer and naming; do not introduce alternatives. <!-- factory -->
- Gates: the repo's lint (eslint incl. `react-hooks`/`jsx-a11y` if configured, or biome), `tsc --noEmit`, and vitest/jest must pass. <!-- factory -->
- No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with untrusted content; if raw HTML is unavoidable, sanitise it with the repo's sanitiser and build `{ __html }` where it is produced. <!-- factory -->
- No secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) in client code or public env vars; everything shipped to the browser is public. <!-- factory -->

## Purity and immutability

<!-- [rules] Components and Hooks must be pure; React calls Components and Hooks; [pure] Keeping Components Pure; [reset] Don't nest component definitions; [deps] Updater functions -->
- Rendering is idempotent and side-effect free: no `new Date()`/`Math.random()`, requests, subscriptions, `document.*` writes or writes to outer variables in the render body.
- Treat props, state, context, hook arguments/returns and values already passed to JSX as read-only; mutating objects created in the same render is fine.
- Replace state with new objects/arrays via the setter (spread, `map`, `filter`); use an updater (`setTodos((prev) => [...prev, todo])`) when the next value depends on the previous.
- Declare components at module top level (one nested in another loses state every render) and render them as JSX, never as `Article()`.
- Never pass hooks as props or wrap them in higher-order hooks. Code must behave identically under Strict Mode's double render and effect re-run.

## Rules of Hooks

<!-- [rules] Rules of Hooks; Strict Mode and linting -->
- Call hooks unconditionally at the top level of components and `use…` custom hooks, before any early `return`; a helper that needs a hook becomes a custom hook.
- Never call hooks in conditions, loops, event handlers, `try`/`catch`/`finally`, or callbacks given to `useMemo`, `useReducer` or `useEffect`.

## State structure

<!-- [state] Choosing the State Structure; [sharing] Sharing State Between Components; [reset] Resetting state with a key; [no-effect] Updating state based on props or state; Resetting all state when a prop changes; Adjusting some state when a prop changes -->
- Compute anything derivable from props or state during render, never store or sync it by effect; don't copy props into state unless named `initialX`/`defaultX`.
- Replace flags that can contradict (`isSending` + `isSent`) with one status union; merge variables that always change together.
- Store selected IDs, not copies of objects, and look them up during render; flatten deeply nested state into ID-keyed maps.
- Give each piece of state one owner; to coordinate siblings, lift it to the closest common parent and pass value plus handler down.
- Reset a subtree's state when its identity changes by rendering it with `key={id}`, not with an effect.
```tsx
const fullName = `${first} ${last}`; // ✅ not useState + useEffect
const selected = items.find((i) => i.id === selectedId); // ✅ ID in state, object derived
<Profile key={userId} userId={userId} />; // ✅ resets state on user change
```

## Effects and data fetching

<!-- [effects] Synchronizing with Effects; Fetching data; [lifecycle] Lifecycle of Reactive Effects; [deps] Removing Effect Dependencies; [no-effect] Sending a POST request; Chains of computations; Notifying parent components; Subscribing to an external store; Fetching data -->
- Use an effect only to synchronise with something outside React (network, browser APIs, timers, non-React widgets); one effect per synchronisation process.
- Code that runs because the user acted (submit, buy, notify parent) goes in the event handler; effects are for "because it was displayed".
- Do not chain effects that set state from other state; compute in render and set all next state in one handler. Use `useSyncExternalStore` for external stores.
- Return a cleanup that undoes the setup (disconnect, unsubscribe, `clearInterval`, `removeEventListener`); never use a ref to make an effect "run once".
- List every reactive value the effect reads (props, state, component-body values); setters and own refs may be omitted; `ref.current` and mutable globals cannot be dependencies.
- Never suppress `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. To drop a dependency, make it non-reactive: move constants outside the component or objects/functions into the effect, depend on primitives, use updaters or `useEffectEvent` (only where the repo's React version provides it).
- Fetch through the repo's existing data layer (e.g. TanStack Query, SWR, router loaders); render loading, error and empty states explicitly. <!-- factory -->
- When fetching in an effect, ignore stale responses in cleanup so an older request cannot overwrite a newer one; extract it into a custom hook.
```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  let ignore = false;
  fetchResults(query).then((r) => {
    if (!ignore) setResults(r);
  });
  return () => {
    ignore = true;
  };
}, [query]);
```

## Lists and keys

<!-- [lists] Rendering Lists; [reset] Preserving and Resetting State -->
- Every element returned from `map()` gets a `key` unique among siblings: a database ID, or one generated when the item is created (`crypto.randomUUID()`).
- Never key by `Math.random()` or values made during render; index keys only for static lists. Use `<Fragment key={id}>` for multi-node items; `key` isn't a prop.

## Memoisation

<!-- [compiler] useMemo: Should you add useMemo everywhere?; [no-effect] Caching expensive calculations -->
- `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`memo` are optimisations only; memoise only when a calculation is measured slow (about 1 ms+ via `console.time`, production build) with rarely changing inputs, the value goes to a `memo` child, or another hook depends on it.
- First remove the cause instead: pass JSX as `children`, keep state local, drop unnecessary effects and dependencies. If the repo uses React Compiler, rely on it.

## Accessibility

<!-- [a11y] No ARIA is better than bad ARIA; [a11y-names] Cardinal rules of naming; [a11y-keyboard] Keyboard interface -->
- Prefer native elements (`button`, `a href`, `input` with `label`) over `div` plus ARIA; a `role` obliges you to implement its keyboard behaviour.
- Every interactive element, dialog and table has a concise accessible name; prefer visible text and `<label htmlFor>`, never `placeholder` or `title` alone.
- Everything usable by pointer works by keyboard; keep a visible focus indicator; no positive `tabIndex`; when a dialog closes or a focused item is removed, move focus to its trigger or the next item.

## Testing

<!-- [rtl] Guiding Principles; [queries] Priority, types of queries, screen; [user-event] Introduction; [rules] Don't dynamically use Hooks (mock the server, not components) -->
- Tests live in `*.test.tsx`, `*.spec.tsx` or `__tests__/` (tester edits only these); every spec scenario has at least one test named after it; no snapshot-only tests. <!-- factory -->
- Test through the rendered DOM as a user would; never assert on component instances, internal state or hook calls.
- Query via `screen`: `getByRole` with `name`, then `getByLabelText`, `getByText`; `getByTestId` only when nothing else fits. If `getByRole` fails, suspect an a11y bug. Use `queryBy*` for absence, `await findBy*` for async content.
- Create `userEvent.setup()` inside the test before rendering and `await` each action; use `fireEvent` only when user-event cannot express it.
- Mock the network with canned server responses (the repo's setup, e.g. MSW), not components or hooks.
```tsx
const user = userEvent.setup();
render(<LoginForm />);
await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: /sign in/i }));
expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(/email is required/i);
```

## Summary

- Code is `cargo fmt` formatted and passes `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`; keep the repo's existing crate layout.
- Return `Result` for expected failures; panic only on broken invariants; no `unwrap` outside tests, `expect("… should …")` for proven invariants.
- Error types implement `Error` + `Display` with lowercase messages; never use `()` as an error type.
- Borrow parameters (`&str`, `&[T]`), take ownership only when stored, and never `clone()` just to satisfy the borrow checker.
- Follow API-guideline naming (C-CASE, `as_`/`to_`/`into_`, no `get_`), keep fields private, use newtypes for domain values.
- Every `unsafe` block has a `// SAFETY:` comment; never block an async task; pass untrusted input as `Command` args.
- Unit tests go in a sibling `tests.rs` (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`), integration tests in `tests/`, named after spec scenarios.

## Formatting and lints

<!-- [style] default style, other style advice; [clippy] allow_attributes_without_reason -->
- Keep the repo's existing crate/workspace layout, module style and dependencies; follow local conventions where they differ from this file. <!-- factory -->
- Format with `cargo fmt --all`; never hand-format against rustfmt. Every warning fails the gates, so code must be clippy-clean. <!-- factory -->
- Use `///` docs placed before attributes, `//!` only for module/crate docs, one combined `#[derive(...)]`, and no `#[path]`.
- Prefer expressions: `let x = if cond { a } else { b };` rather than assigning in each branch.
- Fix lints instead of silencing them; if unavoidable, scope the suppression to one item with a reason: `#[expect(clippy::lint, reason = "…")]` (Rust 1.81+; before that, `#[allow]` with a comment).

## Naming

<!-- [api] C-CASE, C-CONV, C-GETTER, C-ITER, C-CTOR; [style] advice; [clippy] wrong_self_convention, new_without_default -->
- `snake_case` for modules, functions, methods, fields, locals, macros; `UpperCamelCase` for types, traits, variants; `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for consts and statics.
- Acronyms are one word (`HttpClient`, `Uuid`, `parse_url`). Write a reserved word as `r#type` or `type_`, never a misspelling like `typ`.
- Conversions: `as_` is free (borrowed→borrowed), `to_` is costly or produces an owned value, `into_` consumes `self`.
- Getters are named after the field (`name()`, `name_mut()`), not `get_name()`. Iterator methods are `iter`/`iter_mut`/`into_iter`.
- Constructors are associated functions: `new`, `with_*` variants, `from_*` for conversions needing extra args. A public no-arg `new` needs a matching `Default`.

## Types and API shape

<!-- [api] C-COMMON-TRAITS, C-DEBUG, C-DEBUG-NONEMPTY, C-CONV-TRAITS, C-NEWTYPE, C-CUSTOM-TYPE, C-VALIDATE, C-STRUCT-PRIVATE, C-HIDDEN, C-BUILDER, C-DTOR-FAIL; [book-errors] 9.3 custom types for validation -->
- Derive the common traits that fit (`Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash`, `Default`, `Ord`, `Copy` for small values). Every public type has a non-empty `Debug`.
- Implement conversions with `From`/`TryFrom` (and `AsRef`/`AsMut`); never implement `Into`/`TryInto` directly.
- Wrap primitives with domain meaning in newtypes (`struct UserId(u64)`); use enums instead of bare `bool`/`Option` arguments.
- Validate once in the constructor of a type with private fields, then accept that type instead of re-checking raw values.
- Keep struct fields private unless the struct is passive data; expose getters. Default to private or `pub(crate)`; `pub` only for the crate's interface.
- Use a builder for many optional settings: required data in `new`, `&mut self` setters, terminal `build()`; take `self` by value only when building must take ownership.
- `Drop` must not fail or block; offer an explicit `close()` returning `Result` for teardown that can fail.

## Errors

<!-- [api] C-GOOD-ERR; [std-error] Error, source(), message style; [book-errors] 9.2 ? and From; [clippy] result_unit_err -->
- Fallible library functions return a dedicated error type implementing `Debug`, `Display` and `std::error::Error`, and `Send + Sync + 'static`. Never use `()` as the error type, even without a payload.
- `Display` messages are concise, lowercase, without trailing punctuation, and name the failing thing: `failed to read config at /etc/app.toml`.
- When wrapping a lower-level error, expose it via `source()` _or_ print it in `Display`, never both (it would be reported twice).
- Propagate with `?`; implement `From<LowerError>` so `?` converts, or `map_err` into a variant carrying context (path, id, operation).
- Use the error-helper crates the repo already uses (e.g. `thiserror`, `anyhow`); do not add new ones. <!-- factory -->

## Result, panic, unwrap

<!-- [book-errors] 9.3; [std-result] unwrap, expect; [std-error] "expect as precondition"; [clippy] unwrap_used, expect_used -->
- Return `Result` for failures that occur in normal operation (I/O, parsing input, network, missing files), so the caller decides; prefer `?`, `match`, `unwrap_or_else`, `ok_or` over panicking.
- Panic only when a contract or invariant is violated (a bug), and document it under `# Panics`.
- No `unwrap()` outside tests (where panicking fails the test). When you know more than the compiler, use `expect` with a "should" precondition: <!-- factory -->

  ```rust
  let len = u16::try_from(HEADER.len()).expect("HEADER constant should fit in a u16");
  ```

## Ownership and borrowing

<!-- [api] C-CALLER-CONTROL, C-GENERIC; [clippy] ptr_arg, needless_pass_by_value, redundant_clone, unnecessary_to_owned -->
- Take `&str`, `&[T]`, `&Path` rather than `&String`, `&Vec<T>`, `&PathBuf` (clippy `ptr_arg` fails the gate); use generics when only iterating or opening paths:

  ```rust
  fn word_count(text: &str) -> usize          // not &String or String
  fn total(items: &[Item]) -> u64             // not &Vec<Item>
  fn load(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> io::Result<Config>
  ```
- Take a parameter by value only when the function stores or consumes it; never borrow and then clone internally.
- Do not `.clone()`, `.to_owned()` or `.to_string()` a value used once and then dropped; restructure borrows instead.

## Documentation

<!-- [api] C-CRATE-DOC, C-EXAMPLE, C-QUESTION-MARK, C-FAILURE, C-LINK; [clippy] missing_errors_doc, missing_panics_doc, missing_safety_doc -->
- Document every public item; crate docs and public functions get a runnable example that uses `?` (hide the `main` wrapper with `# ` lines); link related items as [`Config::load`].
- Add `# Errors` to public functions returning `Result`, `# Panics` when they can panic, `# Safety` to every `unsafe fn` listing all caller invariants.

## Unsafe

<!-- [unsafe] unsafe operations; [nomicon] safe/unsafe meaning, working with unsafe; [clippy] undocumented_unsafe_blocks, missing_safety_doc; [api] C-SEND-SYNC -->
- Write `unsafe` only when the task requires it; prefer safe std or existing-dependency APIs. Crates without unsafe may declare `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
- Keep each `unsafe` block minimal, with a `// SAFETY:` comment directly above it explaining why every contract holds:

  ```rust
  // SAFETY: `i < self.len` was checked above and `len` never exceeds the allocation.
  let byte = unsafe { *self.ptr.add(i) };
  ```
- Encapsulate unsafe behind a safe API with invariants in private fields; no safe caller may cause UB, even via buggy `Ord`/`Hash` impls. Justify every `unsafe impl Send`/`Sync` the same way.

## Async and concurrency

<!-- [async] spawn_blocking, Blocking and Yielding; [clippy] await_holding_lock; [api] C-DTOR-BLOCK -->
- Use the async runtime the repo already uses. <!-- factory -->
- Never block an async task: no `std::thread::sleep`, blocking `std::fs`/`std::net` I/O or long CPU loops, including in `Drop` impls run there.
- Move bounded blocking work to `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (not cancellable once started); run long-lived loops on a `std::thread`, heavy CPU work on a CPU pool.
- Never hold a `std::sync::MutexGuard` across `.await`; lock inside a short non-async method, or use message passing.

## Security

<!-- [std-command] arg/args, Windows caveats -->
- Run external programs with `Command::new(prog).arg(..)`/`.args(..)`; arguments are passed literally, no shell. Never build `sh -c` strings from input or pass untrusted input to Windows `.bat`/`.cmd` files:

  ```rust
  // don't: Command::new("sh").arg("-c").arg(format!("git log -- {user_path}"))
  Command::new("git").args(["log", "--", user_path]).output()?;
  ```
- Use parameterised queries / bind parameters for SQL; never `format!` input into a query. <!-- factory -->
- Never log secrets, tokens or personal data; give types holding them a hand-written `Debug` that redacts the value. <!-- factory -->

## Tests

<!-- [book-tests] unit tests, private functions, integration tests, tests/common/mod.rs, binary crates; [book-modules] module file paths -->
- Unit tests live in a separate `tests.rs` beside the module, declared in the module file: <!-- factory -->

  ```rust
  #[cfg(test)]
  mod tests; // src/parser.rs -> src/parser/tests.rs; src/lib.rs -> src/tests.rs
  ```
- This deliberately deviates from the Book's inline `mod tests { … }`: the tester agent may only edit `tests/*`, `*/tests/*`, `*/tests.rs`, `benches/*`. <!-- factory -->
- Start `tests.rs` with `use super::*;`; it is still a child module, so private items remain testable.
- Integration tests go in `tests/*.rs` against the public API; shared helpers in `tests/common/mod.rs`. Keep `main.rs` thin, logic in `lib.rs`.
- One behaviour per `#[test]`; every spec scenario maps to at least one test named after it (`fn rejects_expired_token()`). <!-- factory -->

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `tests/*`
- `*/tests/*`
- `*/tests.rs`
- `benches/*`
- `*/benches/*`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `cargo fmt --all --check`
- lint: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- types: `cargo check --all-targets`
- test: `cargo test --workspace`
- testAffected: `cargo test {crates}`

# Swift standard

<!-- Sources:
[api] Swift API Design Guidelines — https://www.swift.org/documentation/api-design-guidelines/

[testing] Swift Testing — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/testing
[xcode] Xcode Build Settings Reference — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/build-settings-reference
-->

## Summary

- Keep the package/plugin layout and deployment target the repository already declares.
- `swiftformat --lint` and `swiftlint` are gates; never suppress a rule without a reason.
- Names read as prose at the call site; types are nouns, methods are verbs, booleans are assertions.
- Prefer values and `let`; use `var` only when mutation is part of the design.
- Handle errors with `throws`/`Result`; do not trap or force-unwrap outside tests and proven invariants.
- Public APIs have documentation comments and explicit access control; implementation stays internal.
- Test behaviour with Swift Testing (or the repo's XCTest suite); one test per spec scenario.

## Layout and access

<!-- [api] Fundamentals; [xcode] Packaging -->
- Keep the repository's existing package and plugin directories; don't introduce a second source root. <!-- factory -->
- One primary type per file, file named after the type; extensions that add protocol conformance live beside it.
- Default to `internal`. Add `public` only for the module's real surface; mark implementation details `private` or `fileprivate`.
- Keep platform code behind `#if os(iOS)` / `#if os(macOS)` and shared code platform-neutral. <!-- factory -->

## Naming and API shape

<!-- [api] Naming; [style] Naming -->
- Types and protocols are `UpperCamelCase`; functions, properties and cases are `lowerCamelCase`.
- Methods read as a sentence at the call site: `move(from:to:)`, not `moveFromTo(_:_:)`.
- Booleans assert a fact: `isEnabled`, `hasPermission`, `canRetry`.
- Omit needless words; the argument label carries the role (`add(_ element:)`, `remove(at:)`).
- Acronyms keep a single case (`URLSession`, `userID`); don't abbreviate domain words.

## Values, optionals and errors

<!-- [api] Fundamentals; [testing] Error Handling -->
- Prefer `let`; use `var` only where mutation is required and scoped.
- Avoid force unwrap (`!`), `try!` and `as!` outside tests; use `guard let`, `if let`, or throw.
- Use `throws` for recoverable failure and typed errors for cases callers branch on; never discard an error.
- `fatalError` only for a broken invariant at startup, with a message naming the invariant. <!-- factory -->

## Concurrency

<!-- [api] Concurrency; [lint] Concurrency rules -->
- Keep UI work on the main actor; mark views and view models `@MainActor` where the framework expects it.
- Use structured concurrency (`async let`, task groups); do not detach a task without an owner and cancellation path.
- Shared mutable state is an actor or guarded by a lock; document the isolation boundary.
- Never block the main actor with file, network or database I/O. <!-- factory -->

## Tauri plugins and iOS/macOS glue

<!-- [xcode] Frameworks; [api] Documentation -->
- A Tauri plugin exposes a typed Rust API; Swift stays behind that boundary and never becomes the public contract.
- Request permission strings and entitlements from the security owner; do not edit capability files here. <!-- factory -->
- Verify the host build and the iOS target compile; report which SDK/target you used. <!-- factory -->

## Testing

<!-- [testing] Test declarations; [lint] Test rules -->
- Use Swift Testing (`@Test`, `#expect`) in new code; keep the repo's XCTest suite where it already exists.
- Test behaviour through the public API; avoid snapshot-only tests and sleeps.
- Name tests after the scenario they cover; one scenario can have several focused tests.
- Keep tests deterministic: inject clocks, file systems and network clients at the boundary. <!-- factory -->

## Formatting and verification

<!-- [format] Rules; [lint] Configuration -->
- `swiftformat --lint` must pass; do not reformat code outside the task.
- `swiftlint lint` must pass with the repository's config; fix the cause instead of adding `// swiftlint:disable`.
- `swift build` (and the iOS target build where relevant) must pass before the task is done. <!-- factory -->

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `*Tests.swift`
- `*/Tests/*`
- `Tests/*`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `swiftformat --lint .`
- lint: `swiftlint lint`
- types: `swift build` (with Package.swift); or `if [ -f project.yml ]; then xcodegen generate; fi && project="$(ls -d *.xcodeproj 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)" && [ -n "$project" ] || { echo "no .xcodeproj in the target directory" >&2; exit 1; } && xcodebuild -project "$project" -scheme "$(basename "$project" .xcodeproj)" build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`

<!-- Sources:

[permissions] Permissions — https://v2.tauri.app/security/permissions/
[scope] Command Scopes — https://v2.tauri.app/security/scope/
[csp] Content Security Policy — https://v2.tauri.app/security/csp/
[config] Configuration Files — https://v2.tauri.app/develop/configuration-files/
[config-ref] Configuration reference — https://v2.tauri.app/reference/config/
[app-manifest] tauri_build::AppManifest — https://docs.rs/tauri-build/latest/tauri_build/struct.AppManifest.html
[mocking] Mock Tauri APIs — https://v2.tauri.app/develop/tests/mocking/
[tauri-test] tauri::test — https://docs.rs/tauri/latest/tauri/test/index.html
[plugin-fs] File System plugin — https://v2.tauri.app/plugin/file-system/
[updater] Updater plugin — https://v2.tauri.app/plugin/updater/
-->

## Summary

- Rust lives in `src-tauri/`: code in `src/lib.rs` and its modules; `src/main.rs` only calls `run()`.
- Commands take serde arguments (camelCase keys in JS) and return `Result<T, E>` where `E` implements `Serialize`.
- Slow commands are `async`; async commands with borrowed arguments such as `State<'_, T>` must return `Result`.
- Use commands for request/response, channels for ordered or large streams, events only for small notifications.
- Grant least privilege: narrow permissions with scopes, per window label, in `src-tauri/capabilities/`; commands still validate their own input.
- Keep `app.security.csp` strict; never use `dangerous…` options to make something work.
- Test command logic in Rust; test the frontend with `mockIPC` from `@tauri-apps/api/mocks` and `clearMocks()` after each test.

## Structure

<!-- [structure]; [config]; [capabilities] Schema Files; [permissions]; [plugin-fs] Setup -->
- Keep the repo's existing layout and module conventions. <!-- factory -->
- Put Rust code in `src/lib.rs` and its modules; `run()` carries `#[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)]`. Leave `src/main.rs` as the call to `run()`.
- Capabilities are JSON or TOML in `src-tauri/capabilities/`; app permission files are TOML in `src-tauri/permissions/`. `gen/schemas` is generated by `tauri-build`: reference it from `$schema`, never edit it.
- Platform files (`tauri.linux.conf.json`, …) merge as JSON Merge Patch: arrays such as `app.windows` are replaced whole, so repeat every entry you keep.
- Add plugins with `tauri add <plugin>` (crate, npm package and default permission together) and register them with `.plugin(…::init())`. Keep `tauri`/`tauri-build` on the CLI's minor version; commit both lockfiles.

## Commands

<!-- [calling-rust] Basic Example, Passing Arguments, Returning Data, Error Handling, Async Commands, Accessing an AppHandle, Invoking Multiple Commands -->
- Commands in a module are `pub`; commands directly in `lib.rs` must not be `pub`. Names are global: keep them unique across modules, and register all in one `generate_handler![…]` (a second `.invoke_handler` replaces the first).
- Rust snake_case parameters arrive as camelCase JS keys: `fn save_note(note_id: u32)` is called as `invoke("save_note", { noteId })`.
- Arguments implement `Deserialize`, return values `Serialize`. Return `tauri::ipc::Response` for large binary data instead of JSON-encoding it.
- Return `Result<T, E>`; `Err` rejects the JS promise. `E` must implement `Serialize`, so give a `thiserror` enum a manual impl (use a `tag = "kind"` form when the UI branches on the error):

```rust
impl serde::Serialize for Error {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, s: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        s.serialize_str(&self.to_string())
    }
}
```

- Non-`async` commands run on the main thread and freeze the UI. Make I/O and heavy work `async fn` (or `#[tauri::command(async)]`).
- An async command with a borrowed parameter must return `Result`: take `String` rather than `&str`, and return `Result` whenever `State<'_, T>` is a parameter.
- Commands taking `AppHandle<R>`/`WebviewWindow<R>` that must run under the mock runtime are generic over `R: tauri::Runtime`.
- Call commands through one typed frontend module per domain, not `invoke("…")` strings in components. <!-- factory -->

## State

<!-- [state] -->
- Register with `app.manage(…)`; read with `State<'_, T>` in commands or `app_handle.state::<T>()` elsewhere. Tauri wraps state in `Arc` already: manage `Mutex<T>`, not `Arc<Mutex<T>>`, and move a cloned `AppHandle` into threads.
- Use `std::sync::Mutex` by default; use the async runtime's `Mutex` only when the guard is held across `.await` (e.g. a DB connection).
- An unmanaged or mistyped `State<'_, T>` fails at runtime, not compile time. Define `type AppState = Mutex<AppStateInner>;` and use the alias everywhere.

## Events and channels

<!-- [calling-frontend] Event System, Channels; [calling-rust] Event System, Channels -->
- Use events (`emit`, `emit_to`, `emit_filter`) for small notifications. Payloads are JSON strings: `Serialize + Clone`, `rename_all = "camelCase"`.
- Use a `tauri::ipc::Channel<T>` command argument for progress, streams or large data; the frontend passes `new Channel<T>()` from `@tauri-apps/api/core`.
- Capabilities do not cover events, and global events reach every listener; send window-private data with `emit_to` (which global `listen` does not receive) or a channel.
- `listen` resolves to an unlisten function: await it, and unlisten on unmount:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  const un = listen<Progress>("download-progress", (e) => setProgress(e.payload));
  return () => {
    un.then((f) => f());
  };
}, []);
```

## Capabilities and permissions

<!-- [security]; [capabilities]; [permissions]; [scope]; [app-manifest]; [plugin-fs] Permissions -->
- One capability file per purpose: `identifier`, `description`, `windows` (labels), `permissions`; `platforms` and `remote.urls` only when needed.
- Once `app.security.capabilities` lists identifiers, unlisted capability files are ignored; add new ones to that list. Labels, not titles, are the boundary; a window in several capabilities gets their union. Avoid `"windows": ["*"]`; give window creation only to privileged windows.
- Prefer single-command permissions (`core:window:allow-set-title`, `fs:allow-read-text-file`) over broad sets. Scoped plugins such as `fs` reject paths no scope allows; `deny` beats `allow`:

```json
{ "identifier": "fs:allow-read-text-file", "allow": [{ "path": "$APPDATA/notes/**" }] }
```

- App commands are callable from every window by default. To gate them, list them with `tauri_build::AppManifest::new().commands(&[…])` in `build.rs` and grant the generated `allow-<command>` permission per capability.
- Use `remote.urls` only for origins you own (on Linux and Android an iframe is indistinguishable from its window). Capabilities do not make command code safe: each command enforces its scope and validates the paths, URLs and ids it receives.

## CSP and config security

<!-- [csp]; [config-ref] SecurityConfig, withGlobalTauri; [updater] Signing updates -->
- Set `app.security.csp` (and `devCsp` if dev differs) as tight as possible; Tauri adds hashes and nonces for bundled assets at compile time.
- No scripts from CDNs or hosts you don't own; add `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` to `script-src` only for Rust/WASM frontends.
- Never set `dangerousDisableAssetCspModification`. Leave `app.withGlobalTauri` false and import from `@tauri-apps/api`. Keep `assetProtocol` off unless needed, then narrowly scoped.
- Only the updater public key goes in `tauri.conf.json`; the private signing key never enters the repo.

## Testing

<!-- [tauri-test]; [mocking]; [calling-rust] Accessing an AppHandle -->
- The tester edits only test files: Rust in sibling `tests.rs` modules and `tests/`, frontend in `*.test.ts(x)`. <!-- factory -->
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test named after it, including each command's error result. Add WebDriver end-to-end tests only where the repo already has them. <!-- factory -->
- Test command logic as plain functions. For IPC-level tests use `tauri::test` (`mock_builder`, `mock_app`, `get_ipc_response`, `assert_ipc_response`): unstable, behind the `tauri` crate's `test` feature.
- When IPC tests are planned, the implementer enables that feature (e.g. under `[dev-dependencies]`); the tester cannot edit `Cargo.toml`. <!-- factory -->
- Frontend: `mockIPC((cmd, args) => …)`, `clearMocks()` in `afterEach`, a `window.crypto` polyfill under jsdom. `mockWindows` fakes labels only; `shouldMockEvents: true` fakes `emit`/`listen`, not `emitTo`.

## Gates in this factory

<!-- factory -->
- Gates run in `src-tauri/`: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo test --workspace` (affected crates when scoped).
- `cargo check` compiles `tauri.conf.json` and the capabilities in, so an unknown permission or broken config fails it; capability-only changes re-run the gates.
- `generate_context!` needs `build.frontendDist` to exist; before compiling, a missing local dir is created empty (read from `tauri.conf.json` only).
- Frontend gates come from its TypeScript/React profile. On Linux the cargo gates need WebKitGTK and Tauri's other system packages.

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `tests/*`
- `*/tests/*`
- `*/tests.rs`
- `benches/*`
- `*/benches/*`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `cargo fmt --all --check`
- lint: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs");try{const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("tauri.conf.json","utf8")).build?.frontendDist;if(typeof d==="string"&&!/^[a-z]+:/i.test(d))fs.mkdirSync(d,{recursive:true})}catch{}'; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- types: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs");try{const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("tauri.conf.json","utf8")).build?.frontendDist;if(typeof d==="string"&&!/^[a-z]+:/i.test(d))fs.mkdirSync(d,{recursive:true})}catch{}'; cargo check --all-targets`
- test: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs");try{const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("tauri.conf.json","utf8")).build?.frontendDist;if(typeof d==="string"&&!/^[a-z]+:/i.test(d))fs.mkdirSync(d,{recursive:true})}catch{}'; cargo test --workspace`
- testAffected: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs");try{const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("tauri.conf.json","utf8")).build?.frontendDist;if(typeof d==="string"&&!/^[a-z]+:/i.test(d))fs.mkdirSync(d,{recursive:true})}catch{}'; cargo test {crates}`

## Summary

- Keep the repo's layout, module system, tsconfig, formatter and linter config; never loosen them or add suppressions to pass a gate.
- Code must pass strict `tsc --noEmit`: no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`; take `unknown` and narrow it before use.
- Avoid `as` casts and non-null `!`; narrow with checks, `?.`, `??`, discriminated unions and exhaustive `never` switches.
- Named exports, ES modules, `import type` for type-only imports; no `namespace`, no `export let`, no `const enum`.
- Throw only `Error` subclasses with `cause`; catch as `unknown`; never leave a promise floating or unawaited in `try`.
- Validate untrusted input at the boundary with the repo's schema library; never build shell or SQL from strings; never log secrets.
- Tests go only in test files; every spec scenario has a test whose name mentions that scenario.

## Working in the repo

<!-- [google-ts] Consistency -->
- Work only on the assigned task in its worktree; do not touch unrelated files or reformat code you did not change. <!-- factory -->
- Where the repo differs from this file (ESM vs CommonJS, naming, enums, layout), follow the repo: first the file, then its directory. <!-- factory -->
- Do not edit `tsconfig*.json`, biome, eslint or prettier config, or `package.json` scripts to make a gate pass. <!-- factory -->

## Compiler strictness

<!-- [tsconfig] strict, noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, useUnknownInCatchVariables, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes; [google-ts] @ts-ignore; [ts-eslint] ban-ts-comment -->
- Code must pass `tsc --noEmit` under the full `strict` family: no implicit `any`, explicit `null`/`undefined` handling, `unknown` catch variables. <!-- factory -->
- If `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on, check indexed reads for `undefined` instead of using `!`; if `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is on, omit optional keys rather than assigning `undefined`.
- Never use `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-nocheck`; `@ts-expect-error` only in tests, with a comment naming the expected error.

## Types

<!-- [dos-donts] General Types; [handbook] Everyday Types, More on Functions: object/unknown/Function, Guidelines for Writing Good Generic Functions; Object Types: readonly; [google-ts] any Type, Wrapper types, Do not use {}, Type inference, Prefer interfaces, Prefer optional over |undefined, Generics, Use readonly; [ts-eslint] no-explicit-any, no-wrapper-object-types, no-unsafe-function-type, no-empty-object-type -->
- Use `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `symbol`, `bigint`, `object`; never `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Symbol`, `Object`, `{}` or `Function` as types.
- Use `unknown` for values of unknown shape (parsed JSON, `catch`, external data) and narrow before use; `any` is not allowed.
- Let inference type locals; annotate parameters and the return types of exported functions.
- Use `interface` for object shapes; use `type` for unions, tuples, mapped and conditional types.
- Write optional fields and params as `name?: T`, not `name: T | undefined`; add `| null` at the use site, not inside a shared alias.
- Every type parameter must relate two or more positions; drop parameters used once and avoid generics that appear only in the return type.
- Mark properties never reassigned after construction `readonly` and take non-mutated arrays as `readonly T[]`; `readonly` is shallow.

## Functions, callbacks, overloads

<!-- [dos-donts] Callback Types, Function Overloads; [handbook] More on Functions: Optional Parameters in Callbacks, Writing Good Overloads, Function; [google-ts] Function declarations, Optional vs default params -->
- Type callbacks whose result is ignored as returning `void`, not `any`; write function types as signatures, e.g. `(e: Event) => void`.
- Make callback parameters required (`(data: Data, ms: number) => void`); callers may still pass a callback taking fewer arguments.
- Prefer one signature with a union or optional trailing params over overloads; overload only when return types differ.
- If overloads are needed, list the most specific first; write one with the maximum callback arity, not one per arity.
- Use function declarations for named functions and arrows for callbacks; pass an options object instead of several optional params.

## Narrowing and unions

<!-- [handbook] Narrowing: typeof type guards, Truthiness narrowing, Using type predicates, Discriminated unions, Exhaustiveness checking; [google-ts] Switch statements; [ts-eslint] switch-exhaustiveness-check -->
- Model variants as discriminated unions with a literal tag (`kind: "ok" | "error"`), not one type with many optional fields.
- Narrow with `typeof`, `instanceof`, `in`, tag checks or `x is T` predicates; `typeof null` is `"object"`, and truthiness drops valid `0` and `""`.
- Every `switch` over a union handles each member and ends with a `default` that assigns to `never`:
```ts
switch (shape.kind) {
  case "circle": return Math.PI * shape.radius ** 2;
  case "square": return shape.side ** 2;
  default: { const unhandled: never = shape; throw new Error(`unhandled shape: ${String(unhandled)}`); }
}
```

## Assertions, literals, enums

<!-- [handbook] Everyday Types: Type Assertions, Non-null Assertion Operator, Literal Inference; Enums: Objects vs Enums, Const enum pitfalls; [google-ts] Type and non-nullability assertions, Type assertions and object literals, Const enums, Type coercion; [ts-eslint] no-non-null-assertion; [ts49] satisfies -->
- Do not use `as T` or postfix `!`; neither is checked at runtime. Narrow, use `?.`/`??`, or validate instead.
- If an assertion is unavoidable, add a one-line comment proving it safe; never write `as unknown as T` without one.
- Type object literals with an annotation (`const cfg: Config = {...}`) or `satisfies`, never `{...} as Config`.
- Use `satisfies` to check a literal yet keep its narrow type: `const routes = {...} satisfies Record<RouteName, string>`.
- In new code prefer an `as const` object plus derived union to `enum`; keep existing enums. Never `const enum`; never coerce enums to boolean.
```ts
export const Status = { Active: "active", Closed: "closed" } as const;
export type Status = (typeof Status)[keyof typeof Status];
```

## Modules

<!-- [google-ts] Exports, Import type, Mutable exports, Export visibility, Use modules not namespaces; [tsconfig] verbatimModuleSyntax; [ts-eslint] no-namespace -->
- Use ES `import`/`export`; no `namespace`, `/// <reference>` or `require` in TypeScript unless the repo is CommonJS.
- Use named exports; add a default export only where a framework requires one. <!-- factory -->
- Import type-only symbols with `import type` (or inline `type`); `verbatimModuleSyntax` requires it.
- Export only what other modules use; never `export let`, expose mutable state through a getter function.

## Values, equality, operators

<!-- [google-ts] Equality checks, Use const and let, Type coercion, Iterating objects, Disallowed features; [ts-eslint] prefer-nullish-coalescing, prefer-optional-chain -->
- Use `===`/`!==`; the only exception is `== null` to match both `null` and `undefined`.
- Use `??` (and `??=`) for defaults, not `||`, which also replaces `0`, `""` and `false`. Use `?.` for optional access.
- Use `const` by default and `let` only when reassigned; never `var`, `eval`, `new Function(string)`, `with` or `debugger`.
- Parse numbers with `Number(x)` and check `Number.isNaN`; no unary `+`, no `parseInt` for base 10.
- Iterate with `for...of` over arrays or `Object.entries()`; no `for...in` on arrays.

## Errors

<!-- [google-ts] Exception handling, Only throw errors, Catching and rethrowing, Empty catch blocks; [tsconfig] useUnknownInCatchVariables; [ts-eslint] only-throw-error, prefer-promise-reject-errors; [node-errors] new Error(message[, options]), error.code -->
- Throw only `new Error(...)` or a subclass; never throw or reject with strings, plain objects or `undefined`.
- Define `Error` subclasses for failures callers must tell apart; pass the original as `{ cause }` when wrapping.
- Treat caught values as `unknown`; narrow with `instanceof` and branch on class or `code`, never on message text.
- Catch only to recover, add context or translate at a boundary; an empty `catch` needs a comment explaining why.
```ts
try {
  await repo.save(order);
} catch (err: unknown) {
  throw new OrderSaveError(`saving order ${order.id} failed`, { cause: err });
}
```

## Async

<!-- [ts-eslint] no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises, return-await, await-thenable; [node-errors] Error propagation and interception -->
- Handle every promise: `await` it, `return` it, or attach `.catch`; `void promise` does not handle a rejection.
- Never pass an `async` function where a `void` callback is expected (`forEach`, event handlers), use a promise as a condition, or spread one.
- Inside `try`, write `return await p` so the `catch`/`finally` sees the rejection.
- Run independent work with `Promise.all`/`Promise.allSettled`; keep dependent awaits sequential in `for...of`.

## Untrusted input and secrets

<!-- [handbook] More on Functions: unknown -->
- Type raw input (HTTP bodies, env, files, `JSON.parse`) as `unknown` and validate it at the boundary with the repo's schema library; derive types from the schema. <!-- factory -->
- Never build shell commands or SQL by string concatenation; pass argument arrays (`execFile`) and parameterised queries. <!-- factory -->
- Never log or put into error messages secrets, tokens, credentials or personal data. <!-- factory -->

## Plain JavaScript repos

<!-- [ts-js] Type-checking JavaScript files; [google-ts] JSDoc type annotations -->
- All rules above apply; where the repo uses `// @ts-check` or `checkJs`, type with JSDoc (`@type`, `@param`, `@returns`, `@typedef`). <!-- factory -->
- In `.ts` files, do not repeat types in JSDoc; the signature carries them.

## Tests

<!-- factory -->
- Put tests only in the repo's test files; the tester agent may edit nothing else. <!-- factory -->
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test whose name mentions the scenario. <!-- factory -->
- Use the repo's runner and file naming; one behaviour per test; mock only process boundaries (network, clock, filesystem). <!-- factory -->

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `*.test.ts`
- `*.test.tsx`
- `*.spec.ts`
- `*.spec.tsx`
- `*.test.js`
- `*.test.jsx`
- `*.spec.js`
- `*/__tests__/*`
- `test/*`
- `tests/*`
- `*/test/*`
- `*/tests/*`

- format: `biome format .` (with biome.json or biome.jsonc); or `prettier --check .` (with .prettierrc or .prettierrc.json or .prettierrc.yaml or .prettierrc.js or prettier.config.js or prettier.config.mjs); or `prettier --check .` (with dependency prettier)
- lint: `biome lint .` (with biome.json or biome.jsonc); or `eslint .` (with eslint.config.js or eslint.config.mjs or eslint.config.cjs or eslint.config.ts or .eslintrc or .eslintrc.json or .eslintrc.js or .eslintrc.cjs)
